title: Automated Acceptance Tester — Cucumber
description: Behaviour-driven acceptance tests in Gherkin syntax.
body:
1. Tool identity. This record is the public-edition reference for Cucumber, a automated acceptance tester. Behaviour-driven acceptance tests in Gherkin syntax. Category: Testing and Quality Assurance.

2. Actual implementation. A working implementation ships inside this record as executable JavaScript (demo.program) and was executed in Node.js; the verified output is stored in demo.output. The demonstration exercises the tool's core behavior: [Cucumber] Scenario: login | Given valid creds | Then dashboard shown => ACCEPTED.

3. Inputs and outputs. This class of tool takes test suites and application builds and produces pass/fail reports and coverage metrics. The demonstration's input is a scenario selector (0-7); its output is the human-readable result line kept in demo.output.

4. Execution instructions. Requires Node.js 18 or later and nothing else. Save demo.program to a file, append a call such as console.log(demoMain(0, 'demo')), and run it with node. No dependencies are installed and no network is used.

5. Tests and examples. This record's demonstration scenario was executed in Node.js and its real output captured in demo.output. Re-running demoMain with the same scenario index reproduces it byte-for-byte.

6. Verification status. The record is marked tested: the shipped program was executed and its output verified. The reference facts about Cucumber are public knowledge presented as reference.

7. Integration. Sibling records in this database document seven more automated acceptance tester implementations. Compatible workflows: verify software quality. The demo runs anywhere Node.js runs and composes with shell pipelines through stdout.
